literal: One's own ally is not, indeed; enmity is twofold; himself is one person; let him take as a pleasant ally one of them.
translation: When a person stands alone without any allies and faces two enemies, let him win over one of those two and make them a pleasant ally.
modern: தனக்குத் துணையாக யாரும் இல்லாதபோது, பகைவர்கள் இருவராக இருக்க, தான் மட்டும் தனியாக இருக்கும் ஒருவன், அந்த இரு பகைவர்களில் ஒருவனைத் தனக்கு இனிய துணையாக ஆக்கிக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet provides a practical strategy for survival and success when facing overwhelming odds. If a person has no supporting allies ('தன்துணை இன்று') and is confronted by two distinct enemies ('பகை இரண்டால்') while being entirely alone ('தான் ஒருவன்'), fighting both simultaneously is disastrous. The wise course of action is to win over one of those two adversaries and turn them into a helpful, pleasant ally ('இன்துணையாக் கொள்க அவற்றின் ஒன்று'). By neutralizing one threat and gaining their support, the individual can successfully manage the remaining opponent.
